university: CUNY Graduate School and University Center

documents.unit: CUNY Board of Trustees (system policy applying to the Graduate Center)
documents.title: CUNY Academic Integrity Policy (2024)
documents.summary: CUNY system-wide integrity policy revised in 2024 to cover AI. It classes unauthorized or uncited AI use as cheating or plagiarism and defers the usage rule to each course syllabus or instructor, then sets reporting and sanction procedures.
documents.stance_why: The policy bans AI use 'without written authorization from the instructor' but also says 'Any use of generative AI tools must be in line with the usage policy for specific assignments as defined in the course of the syllabus', so the allowed/forbidden decision is handed to instructors; no tiers are offered.

units.why: The definition of cheating names "artificial intelligence (AI) systems" among unauthorized aids, so unauthorized AI use is classed as misconduct; P36 fits because it is a classification under the integrity policy.
units.anchor: devices, artificial intelligence (AI) systems, or communication during an academic exercise

units.why: The text lists "Copying from another person or from a generative AI system" as cheating; it is a ban on submitting AI-produced work, so P19 rather than P36, which concerns the misconduct label.
units.anchor: Copying from another person or from a generative AI system
units.frag_end: work submitted for credit or a grade

units.why: Uploading assignments or exams to third-party platforms "beyond those assigned for the class" without professor authorization is defined as cheating; this is about sending assignments to outside platforms, so P20.
units.anchor: uploading work or submitting class assignments or exams to third party platforms and websites
units.frag_end: without the proper authorization of a professor
units.policy: Uploading work or submitting class assignments or exams to third party platforms and websites beyond those assigned for the class, such as commercial homework aggregators, without the proper authorization of a professor is cheating.

units.why: "Any use of generative AI tools must be in line with the usage policy for specific assignments" in the syllabus or from the instructor: the rule is set per course or assignment, so P04.
units.anchor: Any use of generative AI tools must be in line with the usage policy
units.frag_start: Any use of generative AI tools

units.why: The usage policy is "defined in the course of the syllabus and/or communicated by the course instructor", so expectations must be communicated to students; P09 fits.
units.anchor: as defined in the course of the syllabus and/or communicated by the course instructor
units.policy: Usage policy for generative AI on specific assignments is defined in the course syllabus and/or communicated by the course instructor.

units.why: Generating content with AI "without written authorization from the instructor" is cheating: the default is a ban unless the instructor permits in writing, which is a fallback rule (P06) rather than a bare ban (P19).
units.anchor: without written authorization from the instructor
units.policy: Using AI tools, including language models or code generators, to generate content for assignments or exams without written authorization from the instructor is cheating.

units.why: Submitting AI-generated content "as solely your own work" is cheating; this is about ownership of what is submitted (P29), not the generation ban.
units.anchor: Submitting content generated by another person or an AI tool

units.why: Content "generated or altered by AI or digital paraphrasing tools without proper citation" is cheating, so AI-derived content requires citation; P24.
units.anchor: content generated or altered by AI or digital paraphrasing tools without proper citation

units.why: Plagiarism includes copying "an AI tool's actual words or images without the use of quotation marks and citations"; a citation requirement for AI text, P24 over P25 since no citation details are specified.
units.anchor: an AI tool’s actual words or images without the use of quotation marks and citations
units.frag_end: attributing the words to their source

units.why: Unauthorized or uncited AI-generated content is listed as plagiarism, classifying it as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: even when paraphrased, without citing the AI as the source
units.frag_end: citing the AI as the source

units.why: Unauthorized use of electronic devices during an examination "to copy, retrieve, generate or send information" is cheating, covering exam-time AI via devices; P22.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use during an examination of notes, prepared answers

units.why: "generating entire assignments or exam responses using AI without authorization" is a substantial violation that can trigger disciplinary sanctions; this concerns sanction escalation, P37.
units.anchor: generating entire assignments or exam responses using AI without authorization
units.frag_end: by a graduate or professional student
units.policy: Generating entire assignments or exam responses using AI without authorization is an example of a substantial violation, for which the Academic Integrity Officer should seek disciplinary sanctions.

units.why: Violations by "a graduate or professional student" are substantial violations warranting disciplinary sanctions; relevant to this Graduate Center but not AI-specific, coded as sanction escalation (P37).
units.anchor: violations committed by a graduate or professional student

units.why: The opening says penalties include "failing or otherwise reduced grades" and suspension or expulsion; concrete penalties stated in advance (P37).
units.anchor: academic sanctions, such as failing or otherwise reduced grades

units.why: Each college "shall subscribe to an electronic plagiarism detection service"; this is similarity-checking tooling (P40).
units.anchor: Each college shall subscribe to an electronic plagiarism detection service
units.frag_end: faculty should inform students of their use

units.why: The policy must be posted on websites and LMS shells and is "recommended" in syllabi: communicating integrity expectations, P09.
units.anchor: It is recommended that the link also be included in each course syllabus
units.frag_start: The CUNY Policy on Academic Integrity,
units.policy: The CUNY Policy on Academic Integrity must be posted to each college's website with a link in the LMS shell, and it is recommended that the link also be included in each course syllabus.

units.why: Orientation sessions must "incorporate a discussion of academic integrity" for new faculty and students; communicating expectations, not AI-specific, P09 is closest.
units.anchor: shall incorporate a discussion of academic integrity

units.why: A faculty member who suspects a violation "shall review with the student the facts and circumstances" whenever feasible: talking with the student before escalation (P57).
units.anchor: shall review with the student the facts and circumstances of the suspected violation whenever feasible
units.frag_start: A faculty member who suspects that

units.why: Faculty must report incidents on a Faculty Report Form to the Academic Integrity Officer; a reporting step under the integrity process, P36.
units.anchor: shall report such incident on a Faculty Report Form
units.frag_start: a faculty member who concludes that

units.why: Students who deny dishonesty get notice of charges, the right to appear and to present witnesses: a right to respond (P64).
units.anchor: right to appear before the Committee
units.frag_start: These procedures, at a minimum, shall
units.policy: Students who deny academic dishonesty are provided written notice of the charges, the right to appear before the Committee, and the right to present witness statements and/or to call witnesses.

units.why: Students who admit but contest a sanction "may appeal the academic sanction" with a written position and evidence: right to respond (P64).
units.anchor: may appeal the academic sanction through the college’s grade appeal process
units.frag_start: the student may appeal the academic

units.why: Material is destroyed when no violation is found; a fairness protection in integrity cases (P64), not AI-specific.
units.anchor: shall remove all material relating to that incident
units.frag_start: shall remove all material relating to

units.why: Colleges implement the policy and "may adopt its own more specific procedures"; an institution-wide framework with local delegation (P56).
units.anchor: may adopt its own more specific procedures to implement the Policy

units.why: The explanation says the revision is needed because the earlier policy "does not address the advent of Artificial Intelligence"; institution-level purpose statement (P56).
units.anchor: does not address the advent of Artificial Intelligence and its use by students

units.why: "Preparing students to learn from and use AI responsibly and ethically is critical to the University's mission" frames AI use as part of the mission; P44 because it is about preparing students.
units.anchor: Preparing students to learn from and use AI responsibly and ethically is critical
units.frag_end: rigor of the University’s academic programs

units.why: "students must become facile with the use of AI" for careers: a professional-skill rationale (P44).
units.anchor: students must become facile with the use of AI to learn effectively
units.frag_end: careers and lives in the future

units.why: Cheating "undermines educational equity and fairness" is a rationale for integrity rules, but it is not about skill-building (P41) so no type fits; UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: which undermines educational equity and fairness
units.uncovered_note: Fairness rationale for academic integrity rules (unfair advantage over classmates, accreditation risk), not about skill-building.

notes: Graduate Center's own AI guidelines were inaccessible; only the CUNY system policy was coded.
